name: How to Fix Water-Damaged Drywall Around a Bathroom Shower

step.name: Step 1: Identify and resolve the moisture source. Before touching the wallboard, trace where the water is coming from—whether it's leaking plumbing valves, cracked shower tile joints, or missing sealant around your trim. Shut off the water supply or stop shower use immediately so water ceases feeding the drywall core.
step.text: Step 1: Identify and resolve the moisture source. Before touching the wallboard, trace where the water is coming from—whether it's leaking plumbing valves, cracked shower tile joints, or missing sealant around your trim. Shut off the water supply or stop shower use immediately so water ceases feeding the drywall core.

step.name: Step 2: Inspect the wallboard and cut out compromised sections. EPA guidance notes that wallboard may be dried in place only when there is no obvious swelling and seams stay intact; otherwise, it must be removed. Use a utility knife or jab saw to cut back past all soft, swollen, or mold-stained gypsum, exposing the nearest wall studs so you have clean framing to fasten against.

step.name: Step 3: Dry the interior cavity thoroughly. Remove wet insulation and use fans and dehumidifiers to pull moisture from the exposed wood studs and floor plates. Do not rush this drying period; EPA standards emphasize resolving moisture within 24 to 48 hours, and framing must register completely dry before new wallboard is hung.

step.name: Step 4: Fasten moisture-resistant wallboard to framing. Measure the opening precisely and hang moisture-rated board or cement backer board if inside wet zones, adhering to proper framing spacing guidelines. Secure the board firmly with corrosion-resistant drywall screws set just below the paper surface without puncturing the core.

step.name: Step 5: Embed tape and apply joint compound. Apply joint compound to the seams and embed moisture-resistant drywall tape tightly into the mud to avoid air bubbles. Once dried, apply second and third skim coats, feathering each layer outward to create a flat, even plane with the surrounding wall.

step.name: Step 6: Sand smooth and apply specialized primer. Once the compound fully hardens, sand away ridges and wipe off all residual drywall dust. Seal the repair with a dedicated moisture-tolerant primer so moisture won't bleed through your topcoats.
